correctness.rationale: Verified the unique cyclic decomposition p(z)=sum_m z^m Q_m(z^q), the root-of-unity cancellation in L2(mu), and the normalized Beta pushforward. The Jacobi h_j formula, including the j=0 removable-singularity case, gives an exact orthonormal basis. The Gamma quotient has the correct N=0 case and successive differences; Stirling ratios yield the exact exponent. Hypergeometric expansion with a compact-uniform coefficient majorant and h_j^{-1}~2j gives a dominated Riemann-sum limit; all q residue sectors contribute because 2A_m-4m/q=2A_0. Complex compact-uniformity follows from bounds on v=xi^q, conj(eta)^q. The standalone checker compared explicit kernels against independent moment-Gram inversion in four cases, closed center values in four cases, and Bessel-scale convergence in six cases. Finite computations are illustrative; all-parameter proof is analytical. The normalized limit is obtained by dividing the full limit by K(0,0)~B0 N^{2A0}/(A0 Gamma(A0)^2), cancelling the alpha-dependent factor; it is one at the center. An extra numerical target comparison at alpha=-0.3 and 1.3 and two finite-shell normalized comparisons test the alpha cancellation without replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The Jacobi direct-sum reduction and scalar central growth can be obtained with standard classical endpoint tools; neither is presented as an independently novel mechanism. The proposed increment is the entire q-channel locally uniform complex off-diagonal vertex universality, specifically its exact independence from alpha after normalization by K(0,0), for singular q-stars. The inspected primary papers do not state this two-variable normalized law; novelty remains provisional.

value.rationale: A q-ray crossing is a natural singular support where all q cyclic character channels contribute on the same shrinking vertex scale. The exact full two-variable normalized scaling kernel, and its independence from the outer Jacobi weight exponent alpha, provide a substantive universality model for polynomial Christoffel/Bergman kernels at branching singularities; the exact scalar growth is a supporting benchmark derived by classical Jacobi tools rather than the sole contribution. There is no asserted general crossing theorem or perturbative stability.
